issues.legal_issue: A coparcener’s voluntary acceptance of a share substantially smaller than his legal entitlement can constitute a deemed disposition benefiting a relative for estate-duty purposes.
material_facts: A deceased member of a Hindu undivided family received substantially less than the value of the share to which he was legally entitled, and the other coparcener benefited by the difference.
The arrangement was made within two years before the deceased’s death and was treated as a genuine transaction rather than a sham or colourable division.
The beneficiary was a relative of the deceased within the meaning of the Act.
issues.conclusion: The benefit received by the relative, measured by the difference between the share to which the deceased was entitled and the share he actually took, was liable to estate duty.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5, 9 and 27 must be read with the inclusive definition of property and Explanation 2 to section 2(15). Explanation 2 deems the extinguishment, at the deceased’s expense, of a debt or other right to be a disposition in favour of the person benefited, and ‘other right’ is of wide import. The resulting benefit may therefore be treated as property passing on death and, where the beneficiary is a relative and the disposition is not for full consideration, as a gift under section 27. The Court approved Valliammai Achi and applied In re Stratton’s Disclaimer; it distinguished Getti Chettiar, which concerned different language in the Gift Tax Act, and Kancharla Kesava Rao, which concerned section 24.

rule.if: estate_duty_case and deceased_coparcener_took_less_than_entitlement and relative_received_the_difference and disposition_within_two_years

predicates.estate_duty_case: The proceeding concerns the assessment of estate duty on property or a benefit connected with a deceased person.
predicates.deceased_coparcener_took_less_than_entit: A deceased member of a jointly held family estate accepted a share substantially smaller than the share to which he was legally entitled.
predicates.relative_received_the_difference: A relative of the deceased obtained the benefit represented by the difference between the deceased’s entitlement and the share he accepted.
predicates.disposition_within_two_years: The arrangement producing that benefit was made less than two years before the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty case concerns a deceased coparcener who accepted less than his entitlement within two years of death and a relative received the difference, the benefit is subject to estate duty.

issues.legal_issue: For a disposition made within two years before death, its bona fide character does not prevent it from being deemed to pass on death.
material_facts: The dispositions considered by the Court were made within two years before the deceased persons’ deaths.
The Court proceeded on the basis that the arrangements were genuine and not sham or colourable transactions.
issues.conclusion: A disposition within two years before death is caught by section 9 regardless of whether it was bona fide; the bona fide qualification matters to dispositions made two years or more before death.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 provides that property taken under a disposition purporting to operate as an immediate gift is deemed to pass on death if the disposition was not bona fide made two years or more before death. The Court held that the bona fide qualification concerns dispositions made two years or more before death; dispositions within the two-year period are caught by section 9 when read with sections 5 and 27 and Explanation 2 to section 2(15).

predicates.estate_duty_case: The proceeding concerns the assessment of estate duty on property or a benefit connected with a deceased person.
predicates.property_taken_under_disposition: A person obtained property or a benefit under an arrangement made by the deceased that purported to operate immediately.
predicates.disposition_within_two_years: The arrangement was made less than two years before the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: In an estate-duty case, property obtained under an immediate disposition made within two years before death is deemed to pass on death.

issues.legal_issue: Each side should bear its own costs when a case of general public importance resolves conflicting views among High Courts.
material_facts: The legal question had produced conflicting views among several High Courts.
The question was of general public importance and required resolution by the Supreme Court.
The Court allowed one appeal and dismissed the other, but directed the parties in both appeals to bear their own costs throughout.
issues.conclusion: The parties in both appeals were directed to bear their respective costs throughout.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its flexible discretion over costs, noting that a party should not necessarily bear all costs for providing the occasion to settle an important and controversial question of law. It relied on Trustees Port, Bombay in adopting the approach of each party bearing its own costs.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.issue_of_general_public_importance: The appeal presents a legal issue of general public importance requiring authoritative resolution.
predicates.conflicting_high_court_views: Different High Courts have taken conflicting views on the legal issue.

issues.definition: When a Supreme Court appeal presents an issue of general public importance on which High Courts have conflicting views, each party bears its own costs.
